questions.text: I can explain what AI is useful for in my daily work.
I can write clear prompts and improve them when the first result is weak.
I know when to use AI and when not to use it.
I use AI regularly for repeatable tasks, not only for experimentation.
I use AI to improve quality, speed, creativity, or problem-solving.
I have a personal workflow for reviewing and improving AI outputs.
I can identify the time, quality, or other benefit AI creates for me.
I compare my results with how I worked before using AI.
I can describe one AI use case that has made a meaningful difference.
I know what personal, confidential, customer, or company information must not be entered into AI tools.
I verify important AI-generated facts, recommendations, code, or content before using them.
I understand the need for human judgment, attribution, and responsible use of AI.

criticalRisks.text: I have entered confidential, personal, customer, or company information into an AI tool without approval.
criticalRisks.action: Stop using that workflow and confirm the approved AI tools and information-handling rules.

criticalRisks.text: I have submitted AI-generated work without checking whether it is accurate, suitable, or properly attributed.
criticalRisks.action: Add a personal verification checklist before submitting or sharing AI-assisted work.

criticalRisks.text: I use AI outputs as final decisions for important matters without appropriate human judgment.
criticalRisks.action: Keep human review and accountability for important customer, employee, financial, legal, safety, or compliance decisions.

criticalRisks.text: I use AI tools that are not approved for my work or knowingly bypass applicable policy.
criticalRisks.action: Stop the use case and move it to an approved tool and compliant workflow.
